bug_semantics: In generate_key()'s sequential-XOR path for on-disk format versions 8 and 10, the implementation accumulated the initial SHA-256(password || salt) snapshot and every normalized hash/KDF-stage output, including the last stage, then normalized the final chain value and appended it again. Because the final chain value is identical to the already-recorded last-stage snapshot, XOR combines that value with itself and removes the last stage. With exactly one memory-hard KDF and no preceding hash stage, the sole expensive stage disappears and the encryption key reduces to the initial cheap SHA-256 snapshot, so an attacker with the encrypted file can test password guesses offline at SHA-256 speed rather than paying the configured KDF cost. Default configurations are not exploitable because earlier hash/KDF stages remain in the XOR.
flaw_origin: fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e introduced the original 1.4 v10/v8 generate_key() composition path. It correctly recorded each KDF output but then made the false assumption documented by its new comment, 'The sequential result is NOT in the accumulator yet', and appended the last output a second time. The direct parent already had supporting normalization/XOR helpers but had neither use_xor_composition nor xor_accumulator in generate_key(), so it did not contain the vulnerable composition. Commit 4aeea8f95fc8774ff30ca306ab7b8efef6625a7b was excluded as the BIC because its own subject and body identify it as the 1.3 refactor/backport made to match the already-designed 1.4 v10 algorithm.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch> and committer Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-vxf9-vwp6-2w43 identifies affected sequential-XOR format_version 8/10 files, the single-KDF/no-prior-hash exploit preconditions, package range <1.4.6, patched version 1.4.6, mainline fix fdf0c6fc, and 1.4.x backport 1c122790. It also states that patched builds write format_version 13 with xor_mode=sequential and that legacy v8/v10 derivation remains for decryption compatibility, so affected files must be re-encrypted.

git log -L 3210,3212:openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py at fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e attributes all three vulnerable final-append lines directly to that commit: the false 'not in the accumulator' comment, normalize_to_key_length_secure(password, key_length), and xor_accumulator.append(sequential_result). The source object at https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/blob/fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e/openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py#L3210-L3212 contains those lines.

The same BIC source path records SHA-256(password + salt) in xor_accumulator at lines 2297-2306 and records the normalized Argon2 final output at lines 2595-2599. When Argon2 is the only stage, password still holds that Argon2 output at the final append, proving that the two equal snapshots cancel while the initial SHA-256 snapshot survives.

Direct-parent verification: git rev-parse fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e^ returned 5cce56cf73a737ea904251319358973490d851a3. Exact parent-tree searches of openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py found no xor_accumulator and no use_xor_composition; the -L diff is a zero-line-to-three-line addition. Thus the vulnerable generate_key() mechanism is absent in the immediate parent even though that parent contains unused supporting XOR helpers.

All-history -S tracing for xor_accumulator.append(sequential_result) found only fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e on the original 1.4 lineage and 4aeea8f95fc8774ff30ca306ab7b8efef6625a7b on releases/1.3.x. The latter explicitly says it refactors v8 to match the 1.4 v10 algorithm, so it is a backport rather than the origin. No squash/member history was exposed or reconstructable; the BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit whose line history directly owns the flawed block. BIC URL: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e.

Version membership: git tag --contains fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e includes every v1.4 tag from v1.4.0 through v1.4.9. At the last vulnerable release, v1.4.5 (peeled commit 2c0155d36e3f4b0c08504deedaf69d3c02a5dc79), openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py:4113-4115 still appends sequential_result unconditionally. On the legacy branch, v1.3.5 has no XOR composition code while v1.3.6 contains the copied vulnerable append at line 3678; this is the source-history boundary for that backport, while the advisory's package constraint remains <1.4.6.

Fix evidence: mainline commit https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/fdf0c6fcdc027a9fb0a71eb84ea4ac29fd3a69f4 changes openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py so format_version >= 13 skips the redundant final append and routes v13 by explicit xor_mode. git merge-base with the BIC returns the BIC itself, confirming causal ancestry.

Patched-release evidence: direct 1.4.x backport https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/1c122790d6d914909514dbe026d051bc06c50844 is contained by v1.4.6 and later tags but not v1.4.5. v1.4.6 peels to 805ee093ec87b8426235df9077ef8d6bd41f15cb and its openssl_encrypt/modules/crypt_core.py:4185-4194 gates the legacy append behind format_version < 13. Release URL: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/releases/tag/v1.4.6.

BIC-only attribution check: numactl-prefixed git cat-file commit fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e shows a single parent, human author and committer Tobi, and a message ending 'Cross-version compatible with 1.3 v8' with no trailers or AI marker. AI attribution on any fix or later commit was not used for the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by algebra in the original sequential-XOR implementation, not by the later fix or by an incidental move. fdc475f1ea7bb5c303732701c9a992f9b8effe7e is the smallest original commit that joins the previously available helpers into the vulnerable generate_key() path and writes both the per-stage snapshots and redundant final snapshot. Line history assigns the vulnerable append to it, and its immediate parent 5cce56cf73a737ea904251319358973490d851a3 lacks the composition variables and path. The superficially earlier 1.3-line commit is explicitly a compatibility backport of the 1.4 algorithm and therefore is not a BIC under the protocol. The BIC precedes the affected v1.4.0-v1.4.5 releases; v1.4.5 retains the unconditional duplicate append. fdf0c6fcdc027a9fb0a71eb84ea4ac29fd3a69f4 supplies the original mainline correction and 1c122790d6d914909514dbe026d051bc06c50844 directly backports it into v1.4.6, matching the first-party patched boundary. The fix deliberately preserves legacy v8/v10 derivation for compatibility and emits corrected v13 sequential files, so old at-risk files require re-encryption. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI attribution marker. Under BIC-only attribution, the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
